audit_metadata.audit_name: DAY 7 — AUDIT 3: CONTROLLED CLASS-WEIGHTING EFFECT & EXPERIMENTAL INTERPRETATION AUDIT

direct_questions_verdict.Q1_controlled_experimental_variable: YES. Class weighting was isolated as the sole intended independent variable.
direct_questions_verdict.Q2_universal_improvement: NO. In 6 of 9 configurations, weighting degraded or failed to improve sensitivity.
direct_questions_verdict.Q3_differ_by_architecture: YES. CNN sensitivity declined under weighting; SwinUNETR sensitivity increased under Protocol C.
direct_questions_verdict.Q4_architecture_dependent_claim: YES, when framed strictly as an empirical observation on this benchmark.
direct_questions_verdict.Q5_explain_why: PARTIALLY. Plausible optimization mechanisms identified (gradient scaling disruption vs majority local minimum escape), but not exhaustively proven.
direct_questions_verdict.Q6_small_sample_limitation: YES. N=12 locked-test LGG cases means 1 case = 8.33 pp, yielding wide binomial confidence intervals (~ +/- 22%).
direct_questions_verdict.Q7_cv_suggests_additional_validation: YES. High CV variance (0.5055 +/- 0.3274) confirms single-split metrics must be interpreted with caution.
direct_questions_verdict.Q8_justifies_focal_loss: YES. Proving that static weighting fails motivates dynamically modulated loss functions.
direct_questions_verdict.Q9_proves_focal_loss_will_work: NO. It only justifies the research hypothesis.
direct_questions_verdict.Q10_strongest_defensible_conclusion: Static class weighting is not a universal remedy for severe 3D medical class imbalance; it can paradoxically degrade sensitivity in pretrained CNNs while providing modest rescue in randomly initialized Vision Transformers.
